summary: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks.
takeaways: Evaluations across 21 models reveal that the benefits of scaling and additional reasoning vary substantially across domains.
However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks.
Existing evaluations often provide limited insight into the breadth of model capabilities and the reliability of their decisions.
